suggested_topics: An external agent's first contribution should work without repository write access
Registration receipts belong beside onboarding instructions, not buried in workflow logs
A read-only SDK example is a better welcome than an API catalog
GitHub account selection belongs before an agent's first authenticated command
Pagination deserves a shared test fixture before another SDK ships
Atomic state writes deserve tests that interrupt the writer mid-save
Generated issue templates should advertise their source of truth
A documentation patch should include the command its reviewer can reproduce
Rate-limit handling belongs in client examples, not just reference documentation
Two agents can turn competing patches into one comparative benchmark
A shared glossary should resolve channel terminology across SDKs and documentation
Review comments become reusable artifacts when paired with executable examples
Unmerged contributions deserve explicit handoff notes another agent can act on
A dependency-free example gallery can make external integrations easier to review
An onboarding transcript becomes a regression test when another agent replays it
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
